options.C: Set up a policy that uses Nearline storage for 30 days, then moves to Coldline for one year, and then moves to Archive storage for two years.
options.D: Set up a policy that uses Standard storage for 30 days, then moves to Coldline for one year, and then moves to Archive storage for two years.

questions.question:
Your organization has created hundreds of service accounts for different applications hosted on-premises and in other clouds that use Google Cloud APIs. You need to audit the service account keys that were created and identify keys older than 90 days.  
  
What should you do?

options.A: Execute the gcloud asset search-all-resources --scope="organizations/[ORG_ID]" --query="createTime < [DATE_90_DAYS_AGO]" --asset-types="apikeys.googleapis.com/Key" --order-by="createTime" command.
options.B: Execute the gcloud iam service-accounts list --filter="createTime < [DATE_90_DAYS_AGO]" command.
options.C: Execute the gcloud kms keys list --filter="createTime < [DATE_90_DAYS_AGO]" command.
options.D: Execute the gcloud asset search-all-resources --scope="organizations/[ORG_ID]" --query="createTime < [DATE_90_DAYS_AGO]" --asset-types="iam.googleapis.com/ServiceAccountKey" --order-by="createTime" command.

questions.question: You are building an application that stores relational data from users. Users across the globe will use this application. Your CTO is concerned about the scaling requirements because the size of the user base is unknown. You need to implement a database solution that can scale with your user growth with minimum configuration changes. Which storage solution should you use?

options.A: Cloud SQL
options.B: Firestore
options.C: Spanner
options.D: Bigtable

questions.question:
Your company built a mobile game that runs on Google Cloud. Players connect to the game from their personal phones over the Internet, and the game sends UDP packets to update the servers about players' actions during multiplayer sessions. The game's backend can scale across multiple virtual machines (VMs), and you need to expose these VMs behind a single IP address.  
  
What should you do?

options.A: Configure an external proxy Network Load Balancer (SSL proxy) in front of the application servers.
options.B: Configure an internal passthrough Network Load Balancer in front of the application servers.
options.C: Configure an external Application Load Balancer in front of the application servers.
options.D: Configure an external passthrough Network Load Balancer in front of the application servers.

questions.question: You have an application that runs on Compute Engine VM instances in a custom Virtual Private Cloud (VPC). Your company’s security policies only allow the use of internal IP addresses on VM instances and do not let VM instances connect to the internet. You need to ensure that the application can access a file hosted in a Cloud Storage bucket within your project. What should you do?

options.A: Enable private services access on the Cloud Storage bucket.
options.B: Add storage.googleapis.com to the list of restricted services in a VPC Service Controls perimeter and add your project to the list of protected projects.
options.C: Enable Private Google Access on the subnet within the custom VPC.
options.D: Deploy a Cloud NAT instance and route the traffic to the dedicated IP address of the Cloud Storage bucket.

questions.question: You are managing an application deployed on Cloud Run. The development team has released a new version of the application. You want to deploy and redirect traffic to this new version of the application. To ensure traffic to the new version of the application is served with no startup time, you want to ensure that there are two idle instances available for incoming traffic before adjusting the traffic flow. You also want to minimize administrative overhead. What should you do?

options.A: Ensure the checkbox “Serve this revision immediately” is unchecked when deploying the new revision. Before changing the traffic rules, use a traffic simulation tool to send load to the new revision.
options.B: Configure service autoscaling and set the minimum number of instances to 2.
options.C: Configure revision autoscaling for the new revision and set the minimum number of instances to 2.
options.D: Configure revision autoscaling for the existing revision and set the minimum number of instances to 2.

questions.question: You are creating a shell script that contains several gcloud CLI commands to access Google Cloud resources. You want to test the script in your local development environment using a service account in the most secure manner. What should you do?

options.A: Generate an ID token for the service account. Use the token with the gcloud CLI commands.
options.B: Enable service account impersonation, and use the gcloud config set command to use it by default.
options.C: Download the service account key file and save it in a secure location. Set the GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS environment variable to the key file.
options.D: Download the service account key file, and use it to generate an access token. Use the token with the gcloud CLI commands.

questions.question: You have a developer laptop running Ubuntu with the Cloud SDK installed, where the Cloud SDK was installed from the Google Cloud Ubuntu package repository. You want to test your application locally on your laptop using Cloud Datastore. What should you do?

options.A: Export Cloud Datastore data using gcloud datastore export.
options.B: Create a Cloud Datastore index using gcloud datastore indexes create.
options.C: Install the google-cloud-sdk-datastore-emulator component using the apt get install command.
options.D: Install the cloud-datastore-emulator component using the gcloud components install command.

questions.question: The DevOps group in your organization needs full control of Compute Engine resources in your development project. However, they should not have permission to create or update any other resources in the project. You want to follow Google’s recommendations for setting permissions for the DevOps group. What should you do?

options.A: Grant the basic role roles/viewer and the predefined role roles/compute.admin to the DevOps group.
options.B: Create an IAM policy and grant all compute.instanceAdmin.* permissions to the policy. Attach the policy to the DevOps group.
options.C: Create a custom role at the folder level and grant all compute.instanceAdmin.* permissions to the role. Grant the custom role to the DevOps group.
options.D: Grant the basic role roles/editor to the DevOps group.

questions.question: You host a website on Compute Engine. The number of global users accessing your website is expanding rapidly. You need to minimize latency and accommodate user growth across multiple geographical regions. You also want to follow Google-recommended practices while minimizing operational costs. Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)

options.A: Use an external Application Load Balancer in Regional mode.
options.B: Deploy your VMs in multiple Google Cloud regions closest to your users' geographical locations.
options.C: Use a Network Load Balancer.
options.D: Use an external Application Load Balancer in Global mode.
options.E: Deploy all of your VMs in a single Google Cloud region with the largest available CIDR range.

questions.question: Your company has developed a new application that consists of multiple microservices. You want to deploy the application to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), and you want to ensure that the cluster can scale as more applications are deployed in the future. You want to avoid manual intervention when each new application is deployed. What should you do?

options.A: Deploy the application on GKE, and add a HorizontalPodAutoscaler to the deployment.
options.B: Deploy the application on GKE, and add a VerticalPodAutoscaler to the deployment.
options.C: Create a GKE cluster with autoscaling enabled on the node pool. Set a minimum and maximum for the size of the node pool.
options.D: Create a separate node pool for each application, and deploy each application to its dedicated node pool.

questions.question:
You need to create a copy of a custom Compute Engine virtual machine (VM) in order to accommodate an anticipated increase in application traffic resulting from a business acquisition.  
  
What should you do?

options.A: Create a Compute Engine snapshot of your base VM. Create your images from that snapshot.
options.B: Create a Compute Engine snapshot of your base VM. Create your instances from that snapshot.
options.C: Create a custom Compute Engine image from a snapshot. Create your images from that image.
options.D: Create a custom Compute Engine image from a snapshot. Create your instances from that image.

questions.question:
You need to migrate invoice documents stored on-premises to Cloud Storage. The documents have the following storage requirements:  
  
• Documents must be kept for five years.  

• Up to five revisions of the same invoice document must be stored, to allow for corrections.  

• Documents older than 365 days should be moved to lower cost storage tiers.  
  
You want to follow Google-recommended practices to minimize your operational and development costs. What should you do?

options.A: Enable retention policies on the bucket, and use Cloud Scheduler to invoke a Cloud Run function to move or delete your documents based on their metadata.
options.B: Enable retention policies on the bucket, use lifecycle rules to change the storage classes of the objects, set the number of versions, and delete old files.
options.C: Enable object versioning on the bucket, and use Cloud Scheduler to invoke a Cloud Run function to move or delete your documents based on their metadata.
options.D: Enable object versioning on the bucket, use lifecycle conditions to change the storage class of the objects, set the number of versions, and delete old files.

questions.question: You recently received a new Google Cloud project with an attached billing account where you will work. You need to create instances, set firewalls, and store data in Cloud Storage. You want to follow Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.A: Use the gcloud CLI services enable cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com command to enable all resources.
options.B: Use the gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com command to enable Compute Engine and the gcloud services enable storage-api.googleapis.com command to enable the Cloud Storage APIs.
options.C: Open the Google Cloud console and enable all Google Cloud APIs from the API dashboard.
options.D: Open the Google Cloud console and run gcloud init --project in a Cloud Shell.

questions.question: You are building a product on top of Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). You have a single GKE cluster. For each of your customers, a Pod is running in that cluster, and your customers can run arbitrary code inside their Pod. You want to maximize the isolation between your customers' Pods. What should you do?

options.A: Use Binary Authorization and allowlist only the container images used by your customers' Pods.
options.B: Use the Container Analysis API to detect vulnerabilities in the containers used by your customers' Pods.
options.C: Create a GKE node pool with a sandbox type configured to gvisor. Add the parameter runtimeClassName: gvisor to the specification of your customers' Pods.
options.D: Use the cos_containerd image for your GKE nodes. Add a nodeSelector with the value cloud.google.com/gke-os-distribution: cos_containerd to the specification of your customers' Pods.

questions.question:
You have downloaded and installed the gcloud command-line interface (CLI) and authenticated with your Google Account. Most of your Compute Engine instances in your project run in the europe-west1-d zone, and you want to avoid specifying this zone with every CLI command when managing these instances.  
  
What should you do?

options.A: Set the europe-west1-d zone as the default zone using the gcloud config subcommand.
options.B: In the Settings page for Compute Engine under Default location, set the zone to europeג€"west1-d.
options.C: In the CLI installation directory, create a file called default.conf containing zone=europeג€"west1ג€"d.
options.D: Create a Metadata entry on the Compute Engine page with key compute/zone and value europeג€"west1ג€"d.

questions.question: You need to configure a budget alert for the usage of Compute Engine services on one of three Google Cloud projects that you manage, where all three projects are linked to a single billing account. What should you do?

options.A: Verify that you are a Billing Account Administrator (or Billing Account Costs Manager) on the billing account. Select the associated billing account and create a budget and alert for the appropriate project.
options.B: Verify that you are a Billing Account Administrator (or Billing Account Costs Manager) on the billing account. Select the associated billing account and create a budget and a custom alert.
options.C: Verify that you are the project administrator. Select the associated billing account and create a budget for the appropriate project.
options.D: Verify that you are project administrator. Select the associated billing account and create a budget and a custom alert.

questions.question: Your finance team wants to be able to view the billing report for your projects, and you need to ensure this access does not grant them any extra permissions on the project. What should you do?

options.A: Grant the finance team's group the roles/billing.user (Billing Account User) role on the billing account.
options.B: Grant the finance team's group the roles/billing.admin (Billing Account Administrator) role on the billing account.
options.C: Grant the finance team's group the roles/billing.viewer (Billing Account Viewer) role on the billing account.
options.D: Grant the finance team's group the roles/billing.projectManager (Project Billing Manager) role on the projects.

questions.question: You need to deploy an application in Google Cloud using serverless technology. You want to test a new version of the application with a small percentage of production traffic. What should you do?

options.A: Deploy the application to Cloud Run. Use gradual rollouts for traffic splitting.
options.B: Deploy the application to Google Kubernetes Engine. Use Cloud Service Mesh for traffic splitting.
options.C: Deploy the application to Cloud Run functions. Specify the version number in the function name.
options.D: Deploy the application to App Engine. For each new version, create a new service.

questions.question: You manage resources in a Google Cloud project. A new service account will be used to invoke a Cloud Run service. You need permissions to manage the IAM policy of the new service account itself (for example, who can use or impersonate it) while following the principle of least privilege. What should you do?

options.A: Request the roles/iam.serviceAccountAdmin role for your user account.
options.B: Request the roles/run.invoker role for your user account.
options.C: Request the Editor role for your user account.
options.D: Request the Owner role for your user account.

questions.question: You need to set up an autoscaling managed instance group for an HTTPS web application, and you want to ensure that any unhealthy VM instances are automatically recreated. What should you do?

options.A: Create a health check on port 443 and use that when creating the Managed Instance Group.
options.B: Select Multi-Zone instead of Single-Zone when creating the Managed Instance Group.
options.C: In the Instance Template, add the label 'health-check'.
options.D: In the Instance Template, add a startup script that sends a heartbeat to the metadata server.

questions.question: You are the Google Cloud systems administrator for your organization. User A reports receiving an error while trying to access the Cloud SQL database in their Google Cloud project, whereas User B can access the database. You need to troubleshoot User A’s issue while following Google-recommended practices. What should you do first?

options.A: Confirm that network firewall rules are not blocking traffic for User A.
options.B: Verify that User A has the Identity and Access Management (IAM) Project Owner role assigned.
options.C: Review recent configuration changes that may have caused unintended modifications to permissions.
options.D: Review the error message that User A received.

questions.question: You are running a Google Kubernetes Engine cluster with autoscaling enabled to host a new application. You need to expose this application publicly over HTTPS on a public IP address. What should you do?

options.A: Create a Kubernetes Service of type NodePort for your application, and a Kubernetes Ingress to expose this Service via a Cloud Load Balancer.
options.B: Create a Kubernetes Service of type ClusterIP for your application. Configure the public DNS name of your application using the IP of this Service.
options.C: Create a Kubernetes Service of type NodePort to expose the application on port 443 of each node of the Kubernetes cluster. Configure the public DNS name of your application with the IP of every node of the cluster to achieve load-balancing.
options.D: Create a HAProxy pod in the cluster to load-balance the traffic to all the pods of the application. Forward the public traffic to HAProxy with an iptable rule. Configure the DNS name of your application using the public IP of the node HAProxy is running on.

questions.question: You are preparing to deploy a new Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system on Google Cloud. This application keeps the entire database in memory to enable fast data access, and you must provision the most suitable Google Cloud resources for it. What should you do?

options.A: Provision preemptible Compute Engine instances.
options.B: Provision Compute Engine instances with GPUs attached.
options.C: Provision Compute Engine instances with local SSDs attached.
options.D: Provision Compute Engine instances with M1 machine type.

questions.question: You want to host your video encoding software on Compute Engine. Your user base is growing rapidly, and users need to be able to encode their videos at any time without interruption or CPU limitations. You must ensure that your encoding solution is highly available, and you want to follow Google-recommended practices to automate operations. What should you do?

options.A: Deploy your solution on multiple standalone Compute Engine instances, and increase the number of existing instances when CPU utilization on Cloud Monitoring reaches a certain threshold.
options.B: Deploy your solution on multiple standalone Compute Engine instances, and replace existing instances with high-CPU instances when CPU utilization on Cloud Monitoring reaches a certain threshold.
options.C: Deploy your solution to a managed instance group, and increase the number of available instances whenever you see high CPU utilization in Cloud Monitoring.
options.D: Deploy your solution to a managed instance group, and set the autoscaling based on CPU utilization.

questions.question: You have an application that uses Spanner as its backend database. The application experiences a very predictable traffic pattern. You want to automatically scale the number of Spanner nodes up or down depending on the traffic. What should you do?

options.A: Create a cron job that runs on a scheduled basis to review Cloud Monitoring metrics, and then resize the Spanner instance accordingly.
options.B: Create a Cloud Monitoring alerting policy to send an alert to oncall SRE emails when Spanner CPU exceeds the threshold. SREs would scale resources up or down accordingly.
options.C: Create a Cloud Monitoring alerting policy to send an alert to Google Cloud Support email when Spanner CPU exceeds your threshold. Google support would scale resources up or down accordingly.
options.D: Create a Cloud Monitoring alerting policy to send an alert to webhook when Spanner CPU is over or under your threshold. Create a Cloud Run function that listens to HTTP and resizes Spanner resources accordingly.

questions.question: You are diagnosing a complex application failure. In Cloud Logging, you found several unfamiliar, cryptic error messages that contain no personally identifiable information (PII). You need to quickly understand what these logs mean and decide which actions to take. What should you do first?

options.A: Manually copy the error messages, and search for them in public forums and documentation.
options.B: Use Cloud Profiler to analyze the application’s performance during the time of the errors.
options.C: Use the Investigate log option in Logs Explorer to have Gemini Cloud Assist summarize the log entry.
options.D: Search the application source code to determine the cause of the errors.

questions.question: You are auditing your Google Cloud organization. You need to find every Compute Engine instance that has a public IP address. You want a solution that is straightforward to maintain and uses Google Cloud managed services. What should you do?

options.A: Enable the compute.vmExternalIpAccess organization policy at the organization level.
options.B: Use Cloud Shell and Gemini CLI to query the Compute Engine API for instances with a public IP address.
options.C: Use Cloud Asset Inventory to query for all Compute Engine instances with a public IP address.
options.D: Create a shell script using the gcloud CLI to find all instances with a public IP address.

questions.question: Your customer wants you to create a secure website with autoscaling based on the compute instance CPU load. You want to enhance performance by storing static content in Cloud Storage. Which resources are needed to distribute the user traffic?

options.A: A global external Application Load Balancer with a Google-managed SSL certificate to distribute the load and a URL map to target the requests for the static content to the Cloud Storage backend.
options.B: An external passthrough Network Load Balancer pointing to the backend instances to distribute the load evenly. The web servers will forward the request to the Cloud Storage as needed.
options.C: An internal Application Load Balancer together with Identity-Aware Proxy to allow only HTTPS traffic.
options.D: A global external Application Load Balancer to distribute the load and a URL map to target the requests for the static content to the Cloud Storage backend. Install the HTTPS certificates on the instance.

questions.question: You need to add a group of new users to Cloud Identity. Some of the users already have existing Google accounts. You want to follow one of Google's recommended practices and avoid conflicting accounts. What should you do?

options.A: Invite the user to transfer their existing account.
options.B: Invite the user to use an email alias to resolve the conflict.
options.C: Tell the user that they must delete their existing account.
options.D: Tell the user to remove all personal email from the existing account.

questions.question: You want your Cloud Run service to be able to send and consume Pub/Sub messages, but the Pub/Sub API is currently disabled for your project. You plan to use a service account to authenticate your application to the API. You need to ensure your application can use Pub/Sub. What should you do?

options.A: Enable the Pub/Sub API in the API Library on the Google Cloud console.
options.B: Rely on the automatic enablement of the Pub/Sub API when the Service Account accesses it.
options.C: Use Deployment Manager to deploy your application. Rely on the automatic enablement of all APIs used by the application being deployed.
options.D: Grant the Cloud Run service's runtime service account the Pub/Sub Admin role. Have your application enable the API on the first connection to Pub/Sub.

questions.question: Your application stores files on Cloud Storage by using the Standard Storage class. The application only requires access to files created in the last 30 days. You want to automatically save costs on files that are no longer accessed by the application. What should you do?

options.A: Create an object lifecycle on the storage bucket to change the storage class to Archive Storage for objects with an age over 30 days.
options.B: Create a cron job in Cloud Scheduler to call a Cloud Run function every day to delete files older than 30 days.
options.C: Create a retention policy on the storage bucket of 30 days, and lock the bucket by using a retention policy lock.
options.D: Enable object versioning on the storage bucket and add lifecycle rules to expire non-current versions after 30 days.

questions.question: You are running out of primary internal IP addresses in a subnet for a custom mode VPC. The subnet has the IP range 10.0.0.0/20, and the IP addresses are primarily used by virtual machines in the project. You need to provide more IP addresses for the virtual machines. What should you do?

options.A: Add a secondary IP range 10.1.0.0/20 to the subnet.
options.B: Change the subnet IP range from 10.0.0.0/20 to 10.0.0.0/18.
options.C: Change the subnet IP range from 10.0.0.0/20 to 10.0.0.0/22.
options.D: Convert the subnet IP range from IPv4 to IPv6.

questions.question: You lead a team of 10 developers. Each developer has been given their own individual Google Cloud project to use as a personal sandbox for experimenting with different Google Cloud solutions. You want to receive a notification if any developer's spending on their sandbox exceeds $500 in a given month. What should you do?

options.A: Create a single budget for all projects and configure budget alerts on this budget.
options.B: Create a separate billing account per sandbox project and enable BigQuery billing exports. Create a Data Studio dashboard to plot the spending per billing account.
options.C: Create a budget per project and configure budget alerts on all of these budgets.
options.D: Create a single billing account for all sandbox projects and enable BigQuery billing exports. Create a Data Studio dashboard to plot the spending per project.

questions.question:
You create a Deployment with 2 replicas in a Google Kubernetes Engine cluster that has a single Spot VM node pool. After a few minutes, you use `kubectl` to check the status of your Pods and notice that one of them is still showing a Pending status:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783718295874-0wmei56q.jpg)  
  
What is the most likely cause?

options.A: The pending Pod's resource requests are too large to fit on a single node of the cluster.
options.B: Too many Pods are already running in the cluster, and there are not enough resources left to schedule the pending Pod.
options.C: The node pool is configured with a service account that does not have permission to pull the container image used by the pending Pod.
options.D: The pending Pod was originally scheduled on a node that has been preempted between the creation of the Deployment and your verification of the Pods' status. It is currently being rescheduled on a new node.

questions.question: You need to manage a Spanner instance for best query performance. Your instance in production runs in a single Google Cloud region. You need to improve performance in the shortest amount of time. You want to follow Google best practices for service configuration. What should you do?

options.A: Create an alert in Cloud Monitoring to alert when the percentage of high priority CPU utilization reaches 45%. If you exceed this threshold, add nodes to your instance.
options.B: Create an alert in Cloud Monitoring to alert when the percentage of high priority CPU utilization reaches 45%. Use database query statistics to identify queries that result in high CPU usage, and then rewrite those queries to optimize their resource usage.
options.C: Create an alert in Cloud Monitoring to alert when the percentage of high priority CPU utilization reaches 65%. If you exceed this threshold, add nodes to your instance.
options.D: Create an alert in Cloud Monitoring to alert when the percentage of high priority CPU utilization reaches 65%. Use database query statistics to identify queries that result in high CPU usage, and then rewrite those queries to optimize their resource usage.

questions.question: You are developing a new application and need a Jenkins installation to build and deploy your source code. You want to automate the installation as quickly and easily as possible. What should you do?

options.A: Deploy Jenkins through the Google Cloud Marketplace.
options.B: Create a new Compute Engine instance. Run the Jenkins executable.
options.C: Create a new Kubernetes Engine cluster. Create a deployment for the Jenkins image.
options.D: Create an instance template with the Jenkins executable. Create a managed instance group with this template.

questions.question: You are building an application intended to run on Google Kubernetes Engine. You have determined that MongoDB is the best-suited database for this application, and you want to deploy a managed MongoDB environment that comes with a support SLA. What should you do?

options.A: Create a Cloud Bigtable cluster, and use the HBase API.
options.B: Deploy MongoDB Atlas from the Google Cloud Marketplace.
options.C: Download a MongoDB installation package, and run it on Compute Engine instances.
options.D: Download a MongoDB installation package, and run it on a Managed Instance Group.

questions.question: You are creating a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster with the cluster autoscaler feature enabled. You need to ensure that every node in the cluster runs a monitoring pod that sends container metrics to a third-party monitoring solution. What should you do?

options.A: Deploy the monitoring pod in a StatefulSet object.
options.B: Deploy the monitoring pod in a DaemonSet object.
options.C: Reference the monitoring pod in a Deployment object.
options.D: Reference the monitoring pod in a cluster initializer at the GKE cluster creation time.

questions.question:
You are building an application that processes data files uploaded from thousands of suppliers. Your primary goals for the application are data security and the expiration of aged data. You need to design the application so that it:  
  
- Restricts access so that suppliers can access only their own data.  
- Gives suppliers write access to data only for 30 minutes.  
- Deletes data that is over 45 days old.  
  
You have a very short development cycle, and you need to ensure that the application requires minimal maintenance. Which two strategies should you use? (Choose two.)

options.A: Build a lifecycle policy to delete Cloud Storage objects after 45 days.
options.B: Use signed URLs to allow suppliers limited time access to store their objects.
options.C: Set up an SFTP server for your application, and create a separate user for each supplier.
options.D: Build a Cloud Run function that triggers a timer of 45 days to delete objects that have expired.
options.E: Develop a script that loops through all Cloud Storage buckets and deletes any buckets that are older than 45 days.

questions.question: A team of data scientists only occasionally needs to use a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster that you manage. They require GPUs for some long-running jobs that cannot be restarted. You want to minimize cost. What should you do?

options.A: Enable node auto-provisioning on the GKE cluster.
options.B: Create a VerticalPodAutoscaler for those workloads.
options.C: Create a node pool with Spot VMs and GPUs attached to those VMs.
options.D: Create a node pool of instances with GPUs, and enable autoscaling on this node pool with a minimum size of 1.

questions.question: You just installed the Google Cloud CLI on your new corporate laptop. You need to list the existing instances of your company on Google Cloud. What must you do before you run the gcloud compute instances list command? (Choose two.)

options.A: Run gcloud auth login, enter your login credentials in the dialog window, and paste the received login token to gcloud CLI.
options.B: Create a Google Cloud service account, and download the service account key. Place the key file in a folder on your machine where gcloud CLI can find it.
options.C: Download your Cloud Identity user account key. Place the key file in a folder on your machine where gcloud CLI can find it.
options.D: Run gcloud config set compute/zone $my_zone to set the default zone for gcloud CLI.
options.E: Run gcloud config set project $my_project to set the default project for gcloud CLI.

questions.question: Your company closely monitors its cloud spending. You need to enable different teams to monitor their Google Cloud costs. Ensure that team members receive notifications when cloud spend reaches specified thresholds, and allow them to create dashboards for further insights using detailed billing data. You want to follow Google-recommended practices while minimizing engineering costs. What should you do?

options.A: Deploy Grafana to Compute Engine. Create a dashboard for each team that uses the data from the Cloud Billing API. Ask each team to create their own alerts in Cloud Monitoring.
options.B: Set up alerts for each team based on required thresholds. Create a shell script to read data from the Cloud Billing API, and push the results to BigQuery. Grant team members access to BigQuery.
options.C: Deploy Grafana to Compute Engine. Create a dashboard for each team that uses the data from the Cloud Billing Budget API. Ask each team to create their own alerts in Grafana.
options.D: Set up alerts for each team based on required thresholds. Set up billing exports to BigQuery. Grant team members access to BigQuery.

questions.question: You have built an application composed of multiple microservices, with each microservice packaged as its own Docker container image. You want to deploy the whole application on Google Kubernetes Engine in a way that lets each microservice be scaled independently. What should you do?

options.A: Create and deploy a Custom Resource Definition per microservice.
options.B: Create and deploy a Docker Compose File.
options.C: Create and deploy a Job per microservice.
options.D: Create and deploy a Deployment per microservice.

questions.question: Your team has developed a stateless application which requires it to be run directly on virtual machines. The application is expected to receive a fluctuating amount of traffic and needs to scale automatically. You need to deploy the application. What should you do?

options.A: Deploy the application on a managed instance group and configure autoscaling.
options.B: Deploy the application on a Kubernetes Engine cluster and configure node pool autoscaling.
options.C: Deploy the application on Cloud Run functions and configure the maximum number of instances.
options.D: Deploy the application on Cloud Run and configure autoscaling.

questions.question: You are migrating your company’s on-premises compute resources to Google Cloud. You need to deploy batch processing jobs that run every night. The jobs require significant CPU and memory for several hours but can tolerate interruptions. You must ensure that the deployment is cost-effective. What should you do?

options.A: Use the M1 machine series on Compute Engine.
options.B: Containerize the batch processing jobs and deploy them on Compute Engine.
options.C: Use Spot VMs on Compute Engine.
options.D: Use custom machine types on Compute Engine.

questions.question: You are designing an archival solution for your data warehouse and have chosen Cloud Storage to archive the data. Users need to access this archived data about once per quarter to satisfy certain regulatory requirements. You want to choose the most cost-efficient storage option for this use case. Which storage option should you select?

options.A: Coldline Storage
options.B: Nearline Storage
options.C: Regional Storage
options.D: Multi-Regional Storage

questions.question: You have an object stored in a Cloud Storage bucket that contains sensitive data, and you want to share it with an external company. You want access to the content to be revoked after four hours. The external company does not have a Google account that you could use to grant specific user-based access privileges. You want to use the most secure method that requires the fewest steps. What should you do?

options.A: Create a signed URL with a four-hour expiration and share the URL with the company.
options.B: Set object access to 'public' and use object lifecycle management to remove the object after four hours.
options.C: Configure the storage bucket as a static website and furnish the object's URL to the company. Delete the object from the storage bucket after four hours.
options.D: Create a new Cloud Storage bucket specifically for the external company to access. Copy the object to that bucket. Delete the bucket after four hours have passed.

questions.question: You have a virtual machine that is currently configured with 2 vCPUs and 4 GB of memory. It is running out of memory. You want to upgrade the virtual machine to have 8 GB of memory. What should you do?

options.A: Rely on live migration to move the workload to a machine with more memory.
options.B: Use gcloud to add metadata to the VM. Set the key to required-memory-size and the value to 8 GB.
options.C: Stop the VM, change the machine type to n1-standard-8, and start the VM.
options.D: Stop the VM, increase the memory to 8 GB, and start the VM.

questions.question: You are configuring Cloud DNS. You want to create DNS records to point home.mydomain.com, mydomain.com, and www.mydomain.com to the IP address of your Google Cloud load balancer. What should you do?

options.A: Create one CNAME record to point mydomain.com to the load balancer, and create two A records to point WWW and HOME to mydomain.com respectively.
options.B: Create one CNAME record to point mydomain.com to the load balancer, and create two AAAA records to point WWW and HOME to mydomain.com respectively.
options.C: Create one A record to point mydomain.com to the load balancer, and create two CNAME records to point WWW and HOME to mydomain.com respectively.
options.D: Create one A record to point mydomain.com to the load balancer, and create two NS records to point WWW and HOME to mydomain.com respectively.

questions.question: You want to enable your development team to deploy new features to an existing Cloud Run service in production. To minimize the risk associated with a new revision, you want to reduce the number of customers who might be affected by an outage without introducing any development or operational costs to your customers. You want to follow Google-recommended practices for managing revisions to a service. What should you do?

options.A: Ask your customers to retry access to your service with exponential backoff to mitigate any potential problems after the new revision is deployed.
options.B: Gradually roll out the new revision and split customer traffic between the revisions to allow rollback in case a problem occurs.
options.C: Send all customer traffic to the new revision, and roll back to a previous revision if you witness any problems in production.
options.D: Deploy your application to a second Cloud Run service, and ask your customers to use the second Cloud Run service.

questions.question:
You need to assign an Identity and Access Management (IAM) role to an external auditor. The auditor needs permissions to:  
  
- Review your Cloud Audit Logs  
- Review your Data Access logs  
  
What should you do?

options.A: Assign the auditor the IAM role roles/logging.privateLogViewer. Perform the export of logs to Cloud Storage.
options.B: Assign the auditor the IAM role roles/logging.privateLogViewer. Direct the auditor to also review the logs for changes to IAM policy.
options.C: Assign the auditor's IAM user to a custom role that has logging.privateLogEntries.list permission. Perform the export of logs to Cloud Storage.
options.D: Assign the auditor's IAM user to a custom role that has logging.privateLogEntries.list permission. Direct the auditor to also review the logs for changes to IAM policy.

questions.question: Your organization uses Google Workspace for communication and collaboration, and every user in the organization already has a Google Workspace account. You want to grant some of these Google Workspace users access to your Google Cloud project. What should you do?

options.A: Enable Cloud Identity in the Google Cloud console for your domain.
options.B: Grant them the required IAM roles using their Google Workspace email address.
options.C: Create a CSV sheet with all users' email addresses. Use the gcloud command line tool to convert them into Google Cloud accounts.
options.D: In the Google Workspace console, add the users to a special group called cloud-console-users@yourdomain.com. Rely on the default behavior of Google Cloud to grant users access if they are members of this group.

questions.question: You work for a large company that has recently acquired three smaller startups. All Google Cloud resources belonging to the startups must be managed centrally under one Google Cloud organization. However, every startup has its own budget and financial-reporting structure. You need to make sure each startup gets a separate monthly invoice for its Google Cloud usage. What should you do?

options.A: Create a Google Cloud organization with a folder for each startup. Share a single Cloud Billing account, and use the detailed billing export to allocate costs.
options.B: Create a Google Cloud organization with a folder for each startup. Configure each startup to have its own Cloud Billing account.
options.C: Create a Google Cloud organization for each startup. Configure each startup to have its own Cloud Billing account.
options.D: Create a Google Cloud organization for each startup. Share a single Cloud Billing account, and use the detailed billing export to allocate costs.

questions.question: You have received a JSON file containing the private key of a Service Account, which grants access to several resources in a Google Cloud project. After downloading and installing the Cloud SDK, you want to use this private key to authenticate and authorize when running gcloud commands. What should you do?

options.A: Use the command gcloud auth login and point it to the private key.
options.B: Use the command gcloud auth activate-service-account and point it to the private key.
options.C: Place the private key file in the installation directory of the Cloud SDK and rename it to ג€credentials.jsonג€.
options.D: Place the private key file in your home directory and rename it to ג€GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALSג€.

questions.question: You are deploying an application to App Engine. You want the number of instances to scale based on request rate, and you need at least 3 unoccupied (idle) instances available at all times. Which scaling type should you use?

options.A: Manual Scaling with 3 instances.
options.B: Basic Scaling with min_instances set to 3.
options.C: Basic Scaling with max_instances set to 3.
options.D: Automatic Scaling with min_idle_instances set to 3.

questions.question: You have created a new project in Google Cloud through the gcloud command line interface (CLI) and linked a billing account. You need to create a new Compute Engine instance using the CLI. You need to perform the prerequisite steps. What should you do?

options.A: Create a Cloud Monitoring Workspace.
options.B: Create a VPC network in the project.
options.C: Enable the compute.googleapis.com API.
options.D: Grant yourself the IAM role of Compute Admin.

questions.question:
You have an application on a general-purpose Compute Engine instance that is experiencing excessive disk read throttling on its Zonal SSD Persistent Disk. The application primarily reads large files from disk. The disk size is currently 350 GB. You want to provide the maximum amount of throughput while minimizing costs.  

What should you do?

options.A: Increase the size of the disk to 1 TB.
options.B: Increase the allocated CPU to the instance.
options.C: Migrate to use a Local SSD on the instance.
options.D: Migrate to use a Regional SSD on the instance.

questions.question: Your organization has decided to deploy all its compute workloads to Kubernetes on Google Cloud and two other cloud providers. You want to build an Infrastructure-as-code solution to automate the provisioning process for all cloud resources. What should you do?

options.A: Build the solution by using Config Connector, and provision the resources.
options.B: Build the solution by using Terraform, and provision the resources.
options.C: Build the solution by using Python and the cloud SDKs from all providers to provision the resources.
options.D: Build the solution by using YAML manifests, and provision the resources.

questions.question: After a recent security incident, your startup company wants better insight into what is happening in the Google Cloud environment. You need to monitor unexpected firewall changes and instance creation. Your company prefers simple solutions. What should you do?

options.A: Create a log sink to forward Cloud Audit Logs filtered for firewalls and compute instances to Cloud Storage. Use BigQuery to periodically analyze log events in the storage bucket.
options.B: Use Cloud Logging filters to create log-based metrics for firewall and instance actions. Monitor the changes and set up reasonable alerts.
options.C: Install Kibana on a compute instance. Create a log sink to forward Cloud Audit Logs filtered for firewalls and compute instances to Pub/Sub. Target the Pub/Sub topic to push messages to the Kibana instance. Analyze the logs on Kibana in real time.
options.D: Turn on Google Cloud firewall rules logging, and set up alerts for any insert, update, or delete events.

questions.question:
You have a single file containing 32 GB of data that needs to be uploaded to a Nearline Storage bucket. The WAN connection being used is rated at 1 Gbps, and you are the only user on that connection. You want to maximize use of the rated 1 Gbps bandwidth so the file transfers as quickly as possible.  
  
How should you upload the file?

options.A: Use the Google Cloud console to transfer the file instead of gcloud storage.
options.B: Enable parallel composite uploads using gcloud storage on the file transfer.
options.C: Decrease the TCP window size on the machine initiating the transfer.
options.D: Change the storage class of the bucket from Nearline to Multi-Regional.

questions.question: You need to monitor resources that are distributed across different projects in Google Cloud, and you want to consolidate reporting under the same Cloud Monitoring dashboard. What should you do?

options.A: Use Shared VPC to connect all projects, and link Cloud Monitoring to one of the projects.
options.B: For each project, create a Cloud Monitoring metrics scope. In each project, create a service account for that project and grant it the Stackdriver Accounts Editor role in all other projects.
options.C: Configure a single Cloud Monitoring metrics scope, and link all projects to the same scope.
options.D: Configure a single Cloud Monitoring metrics scope for one of the projects. In Cloud Monitoring, create a Group and add the other project names as criteria for that Group.

questions.question: You are developing an application that will be deployed on Google Cloud. The application will use a service account to retrieve data from BigQuery. Before you deploy your application, you want to test the permissions of this service account from your local machine to ensure there will be no authentication issues. You want to ensure that you use the most secure method while following Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.A: Generate a service account key, and configure the gcloud CLI to use this key. Issue a relevant BigQuery request through the gcloud CLI to test the access.
options.B: Grant the service account the BigQuery Administrator IAM role to ensure the service account has all required access.
options.C: Configure the gcloud CLI to use service account impersonation. Issue a relevant BigQuery request through the gcloud CLI to test the access.
options.D: Configure the gcloud CLI with Application Default Credentials using your user account. Issue a relevant BigQuery request through the gcloud CLI to test the access.

questions.question: You need to set up an SSH connection to a single Compute Engine instance for the users in the dev1 group. This instance is the only resource in this particular Google Cloud project that dev1 users should be able to connect to. What should you do?

options.A: Set metadata to enable-oslogin=true for the instance. Grant the dev1 group the compute.osLogin role. Direct them to use the Cloud Shell to ssh to that instance.
options.B: Set metadata to enable-oslogin=true for the instance. Set the service account to no service account for that instance. Direct them to use the Cloud Shell to ssh to that instance.
options.C: Enable block project wide keys for the instance. Generate an SSH key for each user in the dev1 group. Distribute the keys to dev1 users and direct them to use their third-party tools to connect.
options.D: Enable block project wide keys for the instance. Generate an SSH key and associate the key with that instance. Distribute the key to dev1 users and direct them to use their third-party tools to connect.

questions.question:
Company management has asked an external auditor to review all the resources in a specific project. The security team has enabled the Organization Policy called Domain Restricted Sharing on the organization node, specifying only your Cloud Identity domain. You want the auditor to be able to only view — not modify — the resources in that project.  
  
What should you do?

options.A: Ask the auditor for their Google account, and give them the Viewer role on the project.
options.B: Ask the auditor for their Google account, and give them the Security Reviewer role on the project.
options.C: Create a temporary account for the auditor in Cloud Identity, and give that account the Viewer role on the project.
options.D: Create a temporary account for the auditor in Cloud Identity, and give that account the Security Reviewer role on the project.

questions.question:
You operate a data warehouse on BigQuery. A partner company wants to build a recommendation engine using data from your data warehouse. This partner company also runs its own workloads on Google Cloud, managing its resources within its own separate project, but it needs access to the BigQuery dataset that resides in your project.  
  
What should you do to provide the partner company with access to the dataset?

options.A: Create a Service Account in your own project, and grant this Service Account access to BigQuery in your project.
options.B: Create a Service Account in your own project, and ask the partner to grant this Service Account access to BigQuery in their project.
options.C: Ask the partner to create a Service Account in their project, and have them give the Service Account access to BigQuery in their project.
options.D: Ask the partner to create a Service Account in their project, and grant their Service Account access to the BigQuery dataset in your project.

questions.question: You have a development project with custom IAM roles defined. You are creating a new production project and want the same custom IAM roles available in it, using the fewest possible steps. What should you do?

options.A: Use gcloud iam roles copy and specify the production project as the destination project.
options.B: Use gcloud iam roles copy and specify your organization as the destination organization.
options.C: In the Google Cloud console, use the 'create role from role' functionality.
options.D: In the Google Cloud console, use the 'create role' functionality and select all applicable permissions.

questions.question: You need to configure a policy so that video files kept in a specific Cloud Storage bucket that uses Standard storage in a single region are transitioned to Coldline storage after 90 days, and then deleted one year after their creation date. Which approach should you use to set up this policy?

options.A: Use Cloud Storage Object Lifecycle Management using Age conditions with SetStorageClass and Delete actions. Set the SetStorageClass action to 90 days and the Delete action to 275 days (365 - 90).
options.B: Use Cloud Storage Object Lifecycle Management using Age conditions with SetStorageClass and Delete actions. Set the SetStorageClass action to 90 days and the Delete action to 365 days.
options.C: Use gsutil rewrite and set the Delete action to 275 days (365-90).
options.D: Use gsutil rewrite and set the Delete action to 365 days.

questions.question:
You manage a Cloud Run service that aggregates and visualizes data from BigQuery. The service runs as a dedicated service account.  
  
The data that needs to be visualized resides in a different project managed by another team. You do not have access to this project, but you want your application to be able to read data from the BigQuery dataset in it.  
  
What should you do?

options.A: Ask the other team to grant your service account the role of BigQuery Job User.
options.B: Ask the other team to grant your service account the role of BigQuery Data Viewer.
options.C: In IAM of your project, ensure that your service account has the role of BigQuery Data Viewer.
options.D: In IAM of your project, grant a newly created service account from the other team the role of BigQuery Job User in your project.

questions.question: You are working for a startup that was officially registered as a business 6 months ago. As your customer base grows, your use of Google Cloud increases. You want to allow all engineers to create new projects without asking them for their credit card information. What should you do?

options.A: Create a Billing account, associate a payment method with it, and provide all project creators with permission to associate that billing account with their projects.
options.B: Grant all engineers permission to create their own billing accounts for each new project.
options.C: Apply for monthly invoiced billing, and have a single invoice for the project paid by the finance team.
options.D: Create a billing account, associate it with a monthly purchase order (PO), and send the PO to Google Cloud.

questions.question: You have an on-premises data analytics set of binaries that processes data files in memory for about 45 minutes every midnight. The sizes of those data files range from 1 gigabyte to 16 gigabytes. You want to migrate this application to Google Cloud with minimal effort and cost. What should you do?

options.A: Create a container for the set of binaries. Use Cloud Scheduler to start a Cloud Run job for the container.
options.B: Create a container for the set of binaries. Deploy the container to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) and use the Kubernetes scheduler to start the application.
options.C: Upload the code to Cloud Run functions. Use Cloud Scheduler to start the application.
options.D: Lift and shift to a VM on Compute Engine. Use an instance schedule to start and stop the instance.

questions.question: You have a Google Cloud Platform project that contains an App Engine application. The application was originally set up to serve from the us-central region. You now need the application to be served from the asia-northeast1 region instead. What should you do?

options.A: Change the default region property setting in the existing GCP project to asia-northeast1.
options.B: Change the region property setting in the existing App Engine application from us-central to asia-northeast1.
options.C: Create a second App Engine application in the existing GCP project and specify asia-northeast1 as the region to serve your application.
options.D: Create a new GCP project and create an App Engine application inside this new project. Specify asia-northeast1 as the region to serve your application.

questions.question: You are configuring service accounts for an application that spans multiple projects. Virtual machines (VMs) running in the web-applications project need access to BigQuery datasets in the crm-databases project. You want to follow Google-recommended practices to grant access to the service account in the web-applications project. What should you do?

options.A: Grant the web-applications service account the Owner role on the web-applications project and appropriate roles on the crm-databases project.
options.B: Grant the web-applications service account the Owner role on the crm-databases project and on the web-applications project.
options.C: Grant the web-applications service account the Owner role on the crm-databases project and roles/bigquery.dataViewer on the web-applications project.
options.D: Grant the web-applications service account roles/bigquery.dataViewer on the crm-databases project, and only the roles it needs in web-applications.

questions.question: Some employees at your organization have been creating projects on Google Cloud and paying for them using their own personal credit cards, which the company later reimburses. The company now wants to consolidate all of these projects under one new, centralized billing account. What should you do?

options.A: Contact cloud-billing@google.com with your bank account details and request a corporate billing account for your company.
options.B: Create a ticket with Google Support and wait for their call to share your credit card details over the phone.
options.C: In the Google Cloud console, go to Resource Manager and move all projects to the root Organization.
options.D: In the Google Cloud console, create a new billing account and set up a payment method.

questions.question:
You are designing a pipeline to process time-series data. Based on the architecture diagram below, which Google Cloud services belong in boxes 1, 2, 3, and 4?  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783718309206-9l7biwqd.jpg)

options.A: Pub/Sub, Dataflow, Firestore in Datastore mode, BigQuery
options.B: Firebase Messages, Pub/Sub, Spanner, BigQuery
options.C: Pub/Sub, Cloud Storage, BigQuery, Bigtable
options.D: Pub/Sub, Dataflow, Bigtable, BigQuery

questions.question: You need to deploy a single stateless web application with a web interface and multiple endpoints. For security reasons, the web application must be reachable from an internal IP address from your company's private VPC and on-premises network. You also need to update the web application multiple times per day with minimal effort and want to manage a minimal amount of cloud infrastructure. What should you do?

options.A: Deploy the web application on a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Standard cluster with an internal ingress.
options.B: Deploy the web application on Cloud Run with Private Google Access configured.
options.C: Deploy the web application on Cloud Run with Private Service Connect configured.
options.D: Deploy the web application to GKE Autopilot with Private Google Access configured.

questions.question:
You have an application that uses Spanner as a database backend to keep current state information about users. Bigtable logs all events triggered by users. You export Spanner data to Cloud Storage during daily backups.  
  
An analyst asks you to join data from Spanner and Bigtable for specific users. You want to complete this ad hoc request as efficiently as possible.  
  
What should you do?

options.A: Create a Dataflow job that copies data from Bigtable and Cloud Storage for specific users.
options.B: Create a Dataflow job that copies data from Bigtable and Spanner for specific users.
options.C: Create a Dataproc cluster that runs a Spark job to extract data from Bigtable and Cloud Storage for specific users.
options.D: Create two separate BigQuery external tables on Cloud Storage and Bigtable. Use the BigQuery console to join these tables through user fields, and apply appropriate filters.

questions.question: You need to host an application on a Compute Engine instance within a project that is shared with other teams. You want to prevent those other teams from accidentally causing downtime on that application. Which feature should you use?

options.A: Use a Shielded VM.
options.B: Use a Preemptible VM.
options.C: Use a sole-tenant node.
options.D: Enable deletion protection on the instance.

questions.question: Last month your project costs were higher than expected. After investigating, you discovered that a development GKE container generated an unusually large volume of logs, driving up the cost. You want to quickly disable these logs using the fewest possible steps. What should you do?

options.A: 1. Go to the Logs Router in Cloud Logging, and add an exclusion filter for the GKE container resource.
options.B: 1. Go to the Logs Router in Cloud Logging, and add an exclusion filter for the GKE Cluster Operations resource.
options.C: 1. Go to the GKE console, and delete existing clusters. 2. Recreate a new cluster. 3. Clear the option to enable legacy Stackdriver Logging.
options.D: 1. Go to the GKE console, and delete existing clusters. 2. Recreate a new cluster. 3. Clear the option to enable legacy Stackdriver Monitoring.

questions.question: You want to deploy a new containerized application into Google Cloud by using a Kubernetes manifest. You want to have full control over the Kubernetes deployment, and at the same time, you want to minimize configuring infrastructure. What should you do?

options.A: Deploy the application on GKE Autopilot.
options.B: Deploy the application on Cloud Run.
options.C: Deploy the application on GKE Standard.
options.D: Deploy the application on Cloud Run functions.

questions.question: You are planning to migrate your on-premises VMs to Google Cloud. You need to set up a landing zone in Google Cloud before migrating the VMs. You must ensure that all VMs in your production environment can communicate with each other through private IP addresses. You need to allow all VMs in your Google Cloud organization to accept connections on specific TCP ports. You want to follow Google-recommended practices, and you need to minimize your operational costs. What should you do?

options.A: Create individual VPCs per Google Cloud project. Peer all the VPCs together. Apply organization policies on the organization level.
options.B: Create individual VPCs for each Google Cloud project. Peer all the VPCs together. Apply hierarchical firewall policies on the organization level.
options.C: Create a host VPC project with each production project as its service project. Apply organization policies on the organization level.
options.D: Create a host VPC project with each production project as its service project. Apply hierarchical firewall policies on the organization level.

questions.question: A company runs its Linux workloads on Compute Engine instances. The company is about to start working with a new operations partner that does not use Google Accounts. Access to the instances needs to be granted to this operations partner so they can maintain the installed tooling. What should be done?

options.A: Enable Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) for the Compute Engine instances, and add the operations partner as an IAP-secured Tunnel User.
options.B: Tag all the instances with the same network tag. Create a firewall rule in the VPC to grant TCP access on port 22 for traffic from the operations partner to instances with the network tag.
options.C: Set up Cloud VPN between your Google Cloud VPC and the internal network of the operations partner.
options.D: Ask the operations partner to generate SSH key pairs, and add the public keys to the VM instances.

questions.question: You are assigned to maintain a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster named 'dev' that was deployed on Google Cloud. You want to manage the GKE configuration using the command line interface (CLI). You have just downloaded and installed the Cloud SDK. You want to ensure that future CLI commands by default address this specific cluster What should you do?

options.A: Use the command gcloud config set container/cluster dev.
options.B: Use the command gcloud container clusters update dev.
options.C: Create a file called gke.default in the ~/.gcloud folder that contains the cluster name.
options.D: Create a file called defaults.json in the ~/.gcloud folder that contains the cluster name.

questions.question:
You are deploying a new frontend service for an online game. The service uses a micro-frontend architecture and comprises multiple containers that communicate through a service mesh.  
  
You need to control how many compute instances run at any given time. What should you do?

options.A: Create a Compute Engine instance template using a container-optimized virtual machine (VM) instance, and create a startup script that installs Istio service mesh. Deploy the service, and create a managed instance group with a fixed number of instances to run the service.
options.B: Create a Cloud Run service specifying the minimum and maximum number of instances, and configure the service to use Cloud Service Mesh. Deploy all the containers to the service.
options.C: Create a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Autopilot cluster, and enable Cloud Service Mesh. Deploy the service, and use vertical and horizontal Pod autoscaling to control the cluster size.
options.D: Create a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Standard cluster with a node pool that has a fixed number of nodes. Enable Cloud Service Mesh, and deploy the service.

questions.question: You are creating a Linux virtual machine that must connect to Cloud SQL. You have already created a service account with the necessary permissions. You want to ensure that the VM uses this service account instead of the default Compute Engine service account. What should you do?

options.A: When creating the VM in the Google Cloud console, specify the service account under the 'Identity and API Access' section.
options.B: Download a JSON Private Key for the service account. On the Project Metadata, add that JSON as the value for the key compute-engine-service-account.
options.C: Download a JSON Private Key for the service account. On the Custom Metadata of the VM, add that JSON as the value for the key compute-engine-service-account.
options.D: Download a JSON Private Key for the service account. After creating the VM, ssh into the VM and save the JSON under ~/.gcloud/compute-engine-service-account.json.

questions.question: You are running multiple microservices in a Kubernetes Engine cluster. One microservice is rendering images. The microservice responsible for the image rendering requires a large amount of CPU time compared to the memory it requires. The other microservices are workloads that are optimized for n2-standard machine types. You need to optimize your cluster so that all workloads are using resources as efficiently as possible. What should you do?

options.A: Assign the pods of the image rendering microservice a higher pod priority than the other microservices.
options.B: Create a node pool with compute-optimized machine type nodes for the image rendering microservice. Use the node pool with general-purpose machine type nodes for the other microservices.
options.C: Use the node pool with general-purpose machine type nodes for the image rendering microservice. Create a node pool with compute-optimized machine type nodes for the other microservices.
options.D: Configure the required amount of CPU and memory in the resource requests specification of the image rendering microservice deployment. Keep the resource requests for the other microservices at the default.

questions.question: Your development team needs a new Jenkins server for their project. You need to deploy the server using the fewest steps possible. What should you do?

options.A: Download and deploy the Jenkins Java WAR to App Engine Standard.
options.B: Create a new Compute Engine instance and install Jenkins through the command line interface.
options.C: Create a Kubernetes cluster on Compute Engine and create a deployment with the Jenkins Docker image.
options.D: Use GCP Marketplace to launch the Jenkins solution.

questions.question:
Your customer has implemented a solution that uses Spanner and notices some read latency-related performance issues on one table. This table is accessed only by their users using a primary key. The table schema is shown below.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783720872504-kn1tyjxh.png)  
  
You want to resolve the issue. What should you do?

options.A: Remove the profile_picture field from the table.
options.B: Add a secondary index on the person_id column.
options.C: Change the primary key to not have monotonically increasing values.
options.D: Create a secondary index using the following Data Definition Language (DDL): `CREATE INDEX person_id_ix ON Persons (person_id, firstname, lastname) STORING (profile_picture)` ![](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783720875514-uvs1x6dx.png)

questions.question: You are using Deployment Manager to provision a Google Kubernetes Engine cluster. Within that same Deployment Manager deployment, you also need to create a DaemonSet in the cluster's kube-system namespace. You want to accomplish this using the fewest possible services. What should you do?

options.A: Add the cluster's API as a new Type Provider in Deployment Manager, and use the new type to create the DaemonSet.
options.B: Use the Deployment Manager Runtime Configurator to create a new Config resource that contains the DaemonSet definition.
options.C: With Deployment Manager, create a Compute Engine instance with a startup script that uses kubectl to create the DaemonSet.
options.D: In the cluster's definition in Deployment Manager, add a metadata that has kube-system as key and the DaemonSet manifest as value.

questions.question: You manage multiple Google Cloud projects and need access to all logs from the past 60 days. You want to be able to explore and quickly analyze the log contents. Following Google-recommended practices, what should you do to obtain the combined logs for all projects?

options.A: Navigate to Cloud Logging and select resource.labels.project_id="*"
options.B: Create a Cloud Logging export with a sink destination to a BigQuery dataset. Configure the table expiration to 60 days.
options.C: Create a Cloud Logging export with a sink destination to Cloud Storage. Create a lifecycle rule to delete objects after 60 days.
options.D: Configure a Cloud Scheduler job to read from Cloud Logging and store the logs in BigQuery. Configure the table expiration to 60 days.

questions.question: You manage a Google Cloud project containing a critical marketing application. You need to give an external vendor read-only access to the objects stored in one specific Cloud Storage bucket. The vendor must not be able to view any other resources in the project. What should you do?

options.A: Create a custom IAM role with the storage.objects.get permission, and grant the vendor this role on the project.
options.B: Grant the vendor the Storage Object User role on the project.
options.C: Grant the vendor the Storage Object User role on the bucket.
options.D: Grant the vendor the Storage Object Viewer role on the bucket.

questions.question: You hold a Google Cloud account that has access to both a production project and a development project. You want to set up an automated process that lists all Compute Engine instances in both the development and production projects every day. What should you do?

options.A: Create two configurations using gcloud config. Write a script that sets configurations as active, individually. For each configuration, use gcloud compute instances list to get a list of compute resources.
options.B: Create two configurations using gsutil config. Write a script that sets configurations as active, individually. For each configuration, use gsutil compute instances list to get a list of compute resources.
options.C: Go to Cloud Shell and export this information to Cloud Storage on a daily basis.

questions.question:
Your company publishes large files using an Apache web server that runs on a Compute Engine instance. The Apache web server is not the only application running in the project. questions.question:
You store sensitive data in three Cloud Storage buckets and have turned on data access logging for them. You need to check the activity of a specific user across these buckets, using the smallest number of steps possible. Specifically, you want to confirm:

questions.question: Your company has many legacy third-party applications that rely on a shared NFS server for file sharing between these workloads. questions.question: Your application development team has created Docker images for an application that will be deployed on Google Cloud. Add a Cloud Armor Security Policy to the load balancer that allowlists the internal IPs of the MIG's instances. 3. Configure the Compute Engine instance to use the address of the load balancer that has been created.
