questions.question: You need to configure optimal data storage for files stored in Cloud Storage for minimal cost. The files are used in a mission-critical analytics pipeline that is used continually. The users are in Boston, MA (United States). What should you do?

options.A: Configure regional storage for the region closest to the users. Configure a Nearline storage class.
options.B: Configure regional storage for the region closest to the users. Configure a Standard storage class.
options.C: Configure dual-regional storage for the dual region closest to the users. Configure a Nearline storage class.
options.D: Configure dual-regional storage for the dual region closest to the users. Configure a Standard storage class.

questions.question:
You are planning to migrate your on-premises data to Google Cloud. The data includes:  
  
• 200 TB of video files in SAN storage  

• Data warehouse data stored on Amazon Redshift  

• 20 GB of PNG files stored on an S3 bucket  
  
You need to load the video files into a Cloud Storage bucket, transfer the data warehouse data into BigQuery, and load the PNG files into a second Cloud Storage bucket. You want to follow Google-recommended practices and avoid writing any code for the migration. What should you do?

options.A: Use gcloud storage for the video files, Dataflow for the data warehouse data, and Storage Transfer Service for the PNG files.
options.B: Use Transfer Appliance for the videos, BigQuery Data Transfer Service for the data warehouse data, and Storage Transfer Service for the PNG files.
options.C: Use Storage Transfer Service for the video files, BigQuery Data Transfer Service for the data warehouse data, and Storage Transfer Service for the PNG files.
options.D: Use Cloud Data Fusion for the video files, Dataflow for the data warehouse data, and Storage Transfer Service for the PNG files.

questions.question: You are migrating a business critical application from your local data center into Google Cloud. As part of your high-availability strategy, you want to ensure that any data used by the application will be immediately available if a zonal failure occurs. What should you do?

options.A: Store the application data on a zonal persistent disk. Create a snapshot schedule for the disk. If an outage occurs, create a new disk from the most recent snapshot and attach it to a new VM in another zone.
options.B: Store the application data on a zonal persistent disk. If an outage occurs, create an instance in another zone with this disk attached.
options.C: Store the application data on a regional persistent disk. Create a snapshot schedule for the disk. If an outage occurs, create a new disk from the most recent snapshot and attach it to a new VM in another zone.
options.D: Store the application data on a regional persistent disk. If an outage occurs, create an instance in another zone with this disk attached.

questions.question:
Your organization runs numerous Google Cloud services that are consolidated in a single project. Every team also has its own separate projects for testing and development work. The DevOps team requires access to all of the production services so they can carry out their responsibilities. You want to make sure that future changes to Google Cloud products don't end up expanding the DevOps team's permissions over time, and you want to follow Google-recommended practices.  
  
What should you do?

options.A: Grant all members of the DevOps team the role of Project Editor on the organization level.
options.B: Grant all members of the DevOps team the role of Project Editor on the production project.
options.C: Create a custom role that combines the required permissions. Grant the DevOps team the custom role on the production project.
options.D: Create a custom role that combines the required permissions. Grant the DevOps team the custom role on the organization level.

questions.question: You are managing a stateful application deployed on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) that can only have one replica. You recently discovered that the application becomes unstable at peak times. You have identified that the application needs more CPU than what has been configured in the manifest at these peak times. You want Kubernetes to allocate the application sufficient CPU resources during these peak times, while ensuring cost efficiency during off-peak periods. What should you do?

options.A: Enable node auto-provisioning on the GKE cluster.
options.B: Configure a Vertical Pod Autoscaler on the Deployment.
options.C: Configure a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler on the Deployment.
options.D: Enable cluster autoscaling on the GKE cluster.

questions.question: You need to configure application performance monitoring for Google Cloud projects A, B, and C so that everything can be viewed through a single pane of glass. You want to monitor CPU, memory, and disk. What should you do?

options.A: Enable API and then share charts from project A, B, and C.
options.B: Enable API and then give the metrics.reader role to projects A, B, and C.
options.C: Enable API and then use default dashboards to view all projects in sequence.
options.D: Enable the Cloud Monitoring API, and then add projects B and C to the metrics scope of project A.

questions.question: Your company uses Cloud Storage to hold application backup files for disaster recovery purposes. The backups are read only if a disaster occurs, but they must be restorable quickly. Following Google's recommended best practices, which storage option should you choose?

options.A: Standard storage in a multi-region
options.B: Standard storage in a region
options.C: Nearline storage
options.D: Coldline storage

questions.question: Your company is running a critical workload on a single Compute Engine VM instance. Your company's disaster recovery policies require you to back up the entire instance’s disk data every day. The backups must be retained for 7 days. You must configure a backup solution that complies with your company’s security policies and requires minimal setup and configuration. What should you do?

options.A: Configure the instance to use persistent disk asynchronous replication.
options.B: Configure daily scheduled persistent disk snapshots with a retention period of 7 days.
options.C: Configure Cloud Scheduler to trigger a Cloud Run function each day that creates a new machine image and deletes machine images that are older than 7 days.
options.D: Configure a bash script using gsutil to run daily through a cron job. Copy the disk’s files to a Cloud Storage bucket with archive storage class and an object lifecycle rule to delete the objects after 7 days.

questions.question: You plan to run several applications, each on its own Compute Engine instance, within the same project. You want to control, at a more granular level, which service account each instance uses when it calls Google Cloud APIs. What should you do?

options.A: When creating the instances, specify a Service Account for each instance.
options.B: When creating the instances, assign the name of each Service Account as instance metadata.
options.C: After starting the instances, use gcloud compute instances update to specify a Service Account for each instance.
options.D: After starting the instances, use gcloud compute instances update to assign the name of the relevant Service Account as instance metadata.

questions.question: Your company would like to store invoices and other financial documents in Google Cloud. You need to identify a Google-managed solution to store this information for your company. You must ensure that the documents are kept for a duration of three years. Your company’s analysts need frequent access to invoices from the past six months. After six months, invoices should be archived for audit purposes only. You want to minimize costs and follow Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.A: Use Cloud Storage with Object Lifecycle Management to change the object storage class to Coldline after six months.
options.B: Use Cloud Storage with Object Lifecycle Management to change the object storage class to Standard after six months.
options.C: Store your documents on Filestore, and move the documents to Cloud Storage with object storage class set to Coldline after six months.
options.D: Store your documents on Filestore, and move the documents to Cloud Storage with object storage class set to Standard after six months.

questions.question: The sales team has a project named Sales Data Digest that has the ID acme-data-digest. You need to set up similar Google Cloud resources for the marketing team but their resources must be organized independently of the sales team. What should you do?

options.A: Grant the Project Editor role to the Marketing team for acme-data-digest.
options.B: Create a Project Lien on acme-data-digest and then grant the Project Editor role to the Marketing team.
options.C: Create another project with the ID acme-marketing-data-digest for the Marketing team and deploy the resources there.
options.D: Create a new project named Marketing Data Digest and use the ID acme-data-digest. Grant the Project Editor role to the Marketing team.

questions.question:
You need to select and configure compute resources for a set of batch processing jobs. These jobs:  
  
- Take approximately 2 hours to complete  
- Run nightly  
  
You want to minimize service costs. What should you do?

options.A: Select Google Kubernetes Engine. Use a single-node cluster with a small instance type.
options.B: Select Google Kubernetes Engine. Use a three-node cluster with micro instance types.
options.C: Select Compute Engine. Use Spot VM instances of the appropriate standard machine type.
options.D: Select Compute Engine. Use VM instance types that support micro bursting.

questions.question: You have an instance group that you want to load balance. You want the load balancer to terminate the client SSL session. The instance group is used to serve a public web application over HTTPS. You want to follow Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.A: Configure an external Application Load Balancer.
options.B: Configure an internal passthrough Network Load Balancer.
options.C: Configure an external proxy Network Load Balancer with SSL offload (target SSL proxy).
options.D: Configure an external proxy Network Load Balancer (target TCP proxy, no SSL offload).

questions.question: You are developing an application that will run in your own data center and will call Google Cloud services such as Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI, which absorbed AutoML). You have already created a service account that has been granted the appropriate access to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. You need to enable this on-premises application to authenticate to the Google Cloud APIs. What should you do?

options.A: Use the Compute Engine metadata server credentials in your on-premises application.
options.B: Use gcloud to create a key file for the service account that has appropriate permissions.
options.C: Set up Dedicated Interconnect between your data center and Google Cloud to enable authentication for your on-premises applications.
options.D: Go to the IAM & admin console, grant a user account permissions similar to the service account permissions, and use this user account for authentication from your data center.

questions.question: Your company uses BigQuery to store and analyze data. Upon submitting your query in BigQuery, the query fails with a quotaExceeded error. You need to diagnose the issue causing the error. What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.A: Use BigQuery BI Engine to analyze the issue.
options.B: Use the INFORMATION_SCHEMA views to analyze the underlying issue.
options.C: Configure Cloud Trace to analyze the issue.
options.D: Search errors in Cloud Audit Logs to analyze the issue.
options.E: View errors in Cloud Monitoring to analyze the issue.

questions.question: You have deployed an application on a single Compute Engine instance. The application writes logs to disk. Users start reporting errors with the application. You want to diagnose the problem. What should you do?

options.A: Navigate to Cloud Logging and view the application logs.
options.B: Configure a health check on the instance and set a “consecutive successes” Healthy threshold value of 1.
options.C: Connect to the instance’s serial console and read the application logs.
options.D: Install and configure the Ops Agent and view the logs from Cloud Logging.

questions.question: Your company wants to provide engineers with access to explore Google Cloud freely in a sandbox environment. The total budget for testing across your organization is $1,000. You need to ensure that engineers are notified when the budget is about to be reached. You want to automate your solution as much as possible. What should you do?

options.A: Create a separate Cloud Billing account for all sandbox projects. Link a credit card with a limit of $1,000 to this billing account. Ensure all sandbox projects are linked to this new Cloud Billing account.
options.B: Create a Google Cloud Folder and ensure that all sandbox projects are located under that Folder. Create a Budget Alert for $1,000 and scope it to the Folder. Configure an email alert to billing administrators and users once the budget is 90% reached.
options.C: Create an email template reminding people to regularly check their Google Cloud spend. Create a Cloud Run function that sends the email to all the project owners. Create a daily job in Cloud Scheduler that triggers the Cloud Run function. Deploy this solution for each sandbox.
options.D: Configure a billing data export to a BigQuery dataset on the Cloud Billing account. Create a dashboard for all costs related to the sandbox experiments. Share the dashboard with all engineers.

questions.question: Using the gcloud command line in Cloud Shell, you need to generate a list of the APIs that are currently enabled for a Google Cloud project named my-project. What should you do?

options.A: Run gcloud projects list to get the project ID, and then run gcloud services list --project <project ID>.
options.B: Run gcloud init to set the current project to my-project, and then run gcloud services list --available.
options.C: Run gcloud info to view the account value, and then run gcloud services list --account <Account>.
options.D: Run gcloud projects describe <project ID> to verify the project value, and then run gcloud services list --available.

questions.question:
Your company is transitioning from an on-premises environment to Google Cloud. Several development teams currently rely on Cassandra environments as backend databases. Each team requires a development environment that is isolated from the other Cassandra instances used by other teams. You want to complete this move to Google Cloud quickly and with minimal ongoing support effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.A: 1. Build an instruction guide to install Cassandra on Google Cloud. 2. Make the instruction guide accessible to your developers.
options.B: 1. Advise your developers to go to Cloud Marketplace. 2. Ask the developers to launch a Cassandra image for their development work.
options.C: 1. Build a Cassandra Compute Engine instance and take a snapshot of it. 2. Use the snapshot to create instances for your developers.
options.D: 1. Build a Cassandra Compute Engine instance and take a snapshot of it. 2. Upload the snapshot to Cloud Storage and make it accessible to your developers. 3. Build instructions to create a Compute Engine instance from the snapshot so that developers can do it themselves.

questions.question:
You used the gcloud container clusters command to create two Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) clusters: prod-cluster and dev-cluster.  
  
• prod-cluster is a standard cluster.  

• dev-cluster is an Autopilot cluster.  
  
When you run the kubectl get nodes command, you only see the nodes from prod-cluster. Which commands should you run to check the node status for dev-cluster?

options.A: gcloud container clusters get-credentials dev-cluster && kubectl get nodes
options.B: gcloud container clusters update dev-cluster --generate-password && kubectl get nodes
options.C: kubectl config set-context dev-cluster && kubectl cluster-info
options.D: kubectl config set-credentials dev-cluster && kubectl cluster-info

questions.question: Your company plans to migrate data from an on-premises relational database to Google Cloud. The existing database can no longer scale with the growth in users, and the user population is expected to increase rapidly. You need to select a relational database that can scale globally while minimizing management and administrative effort. You also want to follow Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.A: Use Cloud SQL.
options.B: Use Spanner.
options.C: Use Firestore.
options.D: Use BigQuery.

questions.question: Your company’s developers use an automation that you recently built to provision Linux VMs in Compute Engine within a Google Cloud project to perform various tasks. You need to manage the Linux account lifecycle and access for these users. You want to follow Google-recommended practices to simplify access management while minimizing operational costs. What should you do?

options.A: Enable OS Login for all VMs. Use IAM roles to grant user permissions.
options.B: Require your developers to create public SSH keys. Write custom startup scripts to update user permissions.
options.C: Require your developers to create public SSH keys. Make the owner of the public key the root user.
options.D: Enable OS Login for all VMs. Write custom startup scripts to update user permissions.

questions.question: You are reviewing Google Cloud service costs across three separate projects. You need to use this cost data to build service cost estimates by service type, broken down daily and monthly, projected for the next six months, using standard query syntax. What should you do?

options.A: Export your bill to a Cloud Storage bucket, and then import into Bigtable for analysis.
options.B: Export your bill to a Cloud Storage bucket, and then import into Google Sheets for analysis.
options.C: Export your transactions to a local file, and perform analysis with a desktop tool.
options.D: Export your bill to a BigQuery dataset, and then write time window-based SQL queries for analysis.

questions.question:
You need to run a single caching HTTP reverse proxy on Google Cloud for a latency-sensitive website. This particular reverse proxy consumes almost no CPU. You want to provide it with:  
  
- A 30-GB in-memory cache  
- An additional 2 GB of memory for the rest of the processes  
  
You want to minimize cost. How should you run this reverse proxy?

options.A: Create a Memorystore for Redis instance with 32-GB capacity.
options.B: Run it on Compute Engine, and choose a custom instance type with 6 vCPUs and 32 GB of memory.
options.C: Package it in a container image, and run it on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), using n1-standard-32 instances as nodes.
options.D: Run it on Compute Engine, choose the instance type n1-standard-1, and add an SSD persistent disk of 32 GB.

questions.question: You developed a web application that will serve traffic for a local event and expect the traffic volume to be unpredictable. You have containerized the application and now want to deploy it on Google Cloud while minimizing costs. What should you do?

options.A: Deploy the web application as a Cloud Run job.
options.B: Deploy the web application on Google Kubernetes Engine in Standard mode.
options.C: Deploy the web application as a Cloud Run service.
options.D: Deploy the web application on Google Kubernetes Engine in Autopilot mode.

questions.question: You are developing a new version of an application that runs in the App Engine environment. Before fully cutting over to the new version, you want to test it with only 1% of your users. What should you do?

options.A: Deploy a new version of your application in Google Kubernetes Engine instead of App Engine and then use GCP Console to split traffic.
options.B: Deploy a new version of your application in a Compute Engine instance instead of App Engine and then use GCP Console to split traffic.
options.C: Deploy a new version as a separate app in App Engine. Then configure App Engine using GCP Console to split traffic between the two apps.
options.D: Deploy a new version of your application in App Engine. Then go to App Engine settings in GCP Console and split traffic between the current version and newly deployed versions accordingly.

questions.question: Your web application is hosted on Cloud Run and needs to query a Cloud SQL database. Every morning during a traffic spike, you notice API quota errors in Cloud SQL logs. The project has already reached the maximum API quota. You want to make a configuration change to mitigate the issue. What should you do?

options.A: Modify the minimum number of Cloud Run instances.
options.B: Use traffic splitting.
options.C: Modify the maximum number of Cloud Run instances.
options.D: Set a minimum concurrent requests environment variable for the application.

questions.question: You are hosting an application on Compute Engine virtual machines (VMs) in us-central1-a. You want to adjust your design so that it can withstand the failure of a single Compute Engine zone, eliminate downtime, and minimize cost. What should you do?

options.A: • Create Compute Engine resources in us-central1-b. • Balance the load across both us-central1-a and us-central1-b.
options.B: • Create a Managed Instance Group and specify us-central1-a as the zone. • Configure the Health Check with a short Health Interval.
options.C: • Create an external Application Load Balancer. • Create one or more global forwarding rules to direct traffic to your VMs.
options.D: • Perform regular backups of your application. • Create a Cloud Monitoring Alert and be notified if your application becomes unavailable. • Restore from backups when notified.

questions.question: You have an application already running in Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) that consists of multiple pods running on four GKE n1-standard-2 nodes. You need to deploy additional pods that require n2-highmem-16 nodes, and this must be done without any downtime. What should you do?

options.A: Use gcloud container clusters upgrade. Deploy the new services.
options.B: Create a new Node Pool and specify machine type n2-highmem-16. Deploy the new pods.
options.C: Create a new cluster with n2-highmem-16 nodes. Redeploy the pods and delete the old cluster.
options.D: Create a new cluster with both n1-standard-2 and n2-highmem-16 nodes. Redeploy the pods and delete the old cluster.

questions.question: You manage a VPC network in Google Cloud whose subnet is quickly nearing its private IP address capacity. You anticipate that the number of Compute Engine VM instances in the same region will double within a week. You must implement a Google-recommended solution that minimizes operational costs and requires no downtime. What should you do?

options.A: Create a second VPC with the same subnet IP range, and connect this VPC to the existing VPC by using VPC Network Peering.
options.B: Delete the existing subnet, and create a new subnet with double the IP range available.
options.C: Permit additional traffic from the expected range of private IP addresses to reach your VMs by configuring firewall rules.
options.D: Use the Google Cloud CLI tool to expand the primary IP range of your subnet.

questions.question: You created an instance of SQL Server 2017 on Compute Engine to test features in the new version. You want to connect to this instance using the fewest number of steps. What should you do?

options.A: Install a RDP client on your desktop. Verify that a firewall rule for port 3389 exists.
options.B: Install a RDP client in your desktop. Set a Windows username and password in the Google Cloud console. Use the credentials to log in to the instance.
options.C: Set a Windows password in the Google Cloud console. Verify that a firewall rule for port 22 exists. Click the RDP button in the Google Cloud console and supply the credentials to log in.
options.D: Set a Windows username and password in the Google Cloud console. Verify that a firewall rule for port 3389 exists. Click the RDP button in the Google Cloud console, and supply the credentials to log in.

questions.question:
An application produces daily reports on a Compute Engine virtual machine (VM) that resides in the project corp-iot-insights. Your team, which works exclusively in the project corp-aggregate-reports, needs a copy of these daily exports placed in the bucket corp-aggregate-reports-storage.  
  
You want to configure access so that:  
  
- The daily reports generated by the VM become available in the bucket corp-aggregate-reports-storage.  
- The configuration uses as few steps as possible.  
- The approach follows Google-recommended practices.  
  
What should you do?

options.A: Move both projects under the same folder.
options.B: Grant the VM Service Account the role Storage Object Creator on corp-aggregate-reports-storage.
options.C: Create a Shared VPC network between both projects. Grant the VM Service Account the role Storage Object Creator on corp-iot-insights.
options.D: Make corp-aggregate-reports-storage public and create a folder with a pseudo-randomized suffix name. Share the folder with the IoT team.

questions.question: You are developing a new web application that will be deployed on Google Cloud Platform. As part of your release cycle, you want to test updates to your application on a small portion of real user traffic. The majority of the users should still be directed towards a stable version of your application. What should you do?

options.A: Deploy the application on App Engine. For each update, create a new version of the same service. Configure traffic splitting to send a small percentage of traffic to the new version.
options.B: Deploy the application on App Engine. For each update, create a new service. Configure traffic splitting to send a small percentage of traffic to the new service.
options.C: Deploy the application on Kubernetes Engine. For a new release, update the deployment to use the new version.
options.D: Deploy the application on Kubernetes Engine. For a new release, create a new deployment for the new version. Update the service to use the new deployment.

questions.question: You need to manage several Google Cloud projects using as few steps as possible. You want to set up the Google Cloud SDK command-line interface (CLI) so that switching between multiple projects is easy. What should you do?

options.A: 1. Create a configuration for each project you need to manage. 2. Activate the appropriate configuration when you work with each of your assigned Google Cloud projects.
options.B: 1. Create a configuration for each project you need to manage. 2. Use gcloud init to update the configuration values when you need to work with a non-default project
options.C: 1. Use the default configuration for one project you need to manage. 2. Activate the appropriate configuration when you work with each of your assigned Google Cloud projects.
options.D: 1. Use the default configuration for one project you need to manage. 2. Use gcloud init to update the configuration values when you need to work with a non-default project.

questions.question: You manage a web application that must read objects from a shared Cloud Storage bucket. Grant a Cloud Run service access to objects in the existing bucket whose names use the `site1-data/` prefix, while ensuring it can access newly uploaded objects. The solution should take minimal effort to implement and maintain. What should you do?

options.A: Enable fine-grained access control, and configure the uploader to set a per object access control list for the Cloud Run service identity to have the READER role when objects with the site1-data/ prefix are uploaded.
options.B: Create a new bucket to store only objects with the site1-data/ prefix. Grant the Cloud Run service identity the roles/storage.objectViewer IAM role on the project.
options.C: Create a new bucket to store only objects with the site1-data/ prefix. Grant the Cloud Run service identity the roles/storage.objectViewer IAM role on the bucket.
options.D: Enable uniform bucket-level access, and configure an IAM binding on the existing bucket. Grant the Cloud Run service identity the roles/storage.objectViewer IAM role on the bucket with an IAM condition for objects with the site1-data/ prefix.

questions.question: You need to deploy SAP HANA workloads on Compute Engine. The installation needs high-performance data storage, with input/output operations per second (IOPS) often exceeding 200,000. The data must be stored on durable block storage that persists independently of the VM, including when the VM is stopped and started again. What should you do?

options.A: Use Hyperdisk Extreme disks for the application data.
options.B: Use in-memory RAM disks for the application data.
options.C: Use Local SSD disks for the application data.
options.D: Use Hyperdisk Throughput disks for the application data.

questions.question: You plan to manage all your Google Cloud resources using Terraform. You have multiple applications that you want to manage independently. You need to organize your Terraform code repository to support this separation. What should you do?

options.A: Create a single module for each resource type, and place all modules in the same directory.
options.B: Put the Terraform configuration resources for each application in its own root directory.
options.C: Create a single module for each application, and place all modules in the same directory.
options.D: Put resources of the same type in their own root directory.

questions.question: You are creating a Compute Engine virtual machine (VM) instance for a new application. Your organization’s policy forbids assigning external IP addresses to VM instances for security reasons. However, the application running on the instance must access the internet to download required software updates and packages. What should you do?

options.A: Set up a VPC Network Peering connection between your VPC network and a VPC network with internet access.
options.B: Create a bastion host with an external IP address, and use it to connect to the VM using SSH.
options.C: Assign an internal static IP address to the VM.
options.D: Configure Cloud NAT for the subnet that the VM is in.

questions.question:
You use the `gcloud container clusters create app-cluster` command to deploy a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster in a new Google Cloud project. The command fails with the following error:  
  
```text  
ERROR: (gcloud.container.clusters.create) ResponseError: code=403, message=Kubernetes Engine API has not been used in the project before or it is disabled.  
```  
  
You need to fix the issue. What should you do?

options.A: Rerun the command with the --enable-autoprovisioning flag.
options.B: Disable the “Require enabling Workload Identity Federation for GKE” organization policy, and then run the cluster creation command again.
options.C: Add the Kubernetes Engine Admin IAM role to your user account, and then run the cluster creation command again.
options.D: Run the gcloud services enable container.googleapis.com command, and then run the cluster creation command again.

questions.question: Your company uses Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) for every application deployment. Your team must provision and manage other Google Cloud resources with the same declarative approach and tooling used for application deployments. What should you do?

options.A: Use the Google Cloud console to provision and manage Google Cloud resources.
options.B: Write shell scripts using gcloud commands to provision and manage Google Cloud resources.
options.C: Create Terraform configurations for your Google Cloud resources, and store the state file in a Cloud Storage bucket.
options.D: Install Config Connector in a GKE cluster, and define your Google Cloud resources as custom resources in Kubernetes manifests.

questions.question: You administer your company’s Google Cloud environment. Your company has a budget and wants to centralize cost management by consolidating every project under one Cloud Billing account. The finance team needs a daily export of all billing data to a central BigQuery dataset for analysis, including resource-level cost data. You must implement the most cost-effective solution with minimal administrative overhead. What should you do?

options.A: Link each project to the Cloud Billing account. Create a new Cloud Billing budget alert with Pub/Sub as the destination, and use a Cloud Run function to write the alerts to BigQuery.
options.B: Link each project to the Cloud Billing account. Enable the standard and detailed usage cost exports on the billing account, specifying a BigQuery dataset as the destination.
options.C: Link each project to the Cloud Billing account. Enable the standard usage cost export on the billing account, specifying a BigQuery dataset as the destination.
options.D: Link each project to the Cloud Billing account. Use the gcloud billing budgets create command to set a budget for each project, and then use the cost breakdown report in the Google Cloud console to manually export the daily costs.

questions.question:
You manage your company's archival records in a Cloud Storage bucket that uses the Multi-Regional storage class. These objects are seldom accessed after 90 days but must be kept indefinitely for regulatory compliance.  
  
You need a cost-effective process that automatically moves these objects to the lowest-cost storage class appropriate for long-term retention immediately after the 90-day period. What should you do?

options.A: Enable Object Versioning on the bucket, and create an Object Lifecycle Management rule that sets the daysSinceNoncurrentTime condition to 90 days, transitioning noncurrent versions to Archive storage.
options.B: Create an Object Lifecycle Management rule on the bucket that specifies an age condition of 90 days and uses the SetStorageClass action to transition the objects to Archive storage.
options.C: Create a nightly scheduled Cloud Run function that uses the Cloud Storage API to change the storage class of all objects older than 90 days to Archive storage.
options.D: Create an Object Lifecycle Management rule on the bucket that specifies the createdBefore condition set to 90 days ago and uses the Delete action to remove the objects.

questions.question:
You are setting up an isolated Google Cloud environment for a new data science team. The team must experiment with machine learning models in short-lived projects and needs full administrative access. All team members are in the same group.  
  
Your solution must limit resource creation to the `us-east1` region and permit only BigQuery and Cloud Storage. What should you do?

options.A: Create a new folder. Create an organization policy with constraints to restrict resource locations and allowed services, and apply it to the folder. Grant the Owner IAM role to the group at the folder level.
options.B: Create a new folder. Create an organization policy with constraints to restrict resource locations and allowed services, and apply it to the folder. Grant the BigQuery Admin and Storage Admin IAM roles to the group at the folder level.
options.C: Create a new folder. Create an organization policy with constraints to restrict resource locations, and apply it to the folder. Grant the Owner IAM role to the group at the folder level.
options.D: Create a new folder. Create an organization policy with constraints to restrict resource locations, and apply it to the folder. Grant the BigQuery Admin and Storage Admin IAM roles to the group at the folder level.

questions.question: You are a Cloud Billing administrator for your organization. Your organization uses many Google Cloud projects and must implement a cost-control mechanism. Project teams need to be notified promptly as their spending nears its limit. You need to deliver near-real-time notifications to a team’s Slack channel when its project’s spending reaches a predefined budget threshold. The solution must be simple to support and require minimal maintenance. What should you do?

options.A: Create a detailed billing export to BigQuery. Create a Cloud Composer directed acyclic graph (DAG) that runs on a schedule to analyze the BigQuery data and post notifications to Slack.
options.B: Create a programmatic budget notification to send messages to a Pub/Sub topic. Create a Cloud Run function that is triggered by messages on the topic and posts the notifications to Slack.
options.C: Create a programmatic budget notification to send messages to a Pub/Sub topic. Create a Compute Engine managed instance group to pull messages from the Pub/Sub subscription and post them to Slack.
options.D: Create a detailed billing export to BigQuery. Create a Cloud Scheduler job that triggers a Cloud Run function to analyze the BigQuery data and post notifications to Slack.

questions.question: Your team manages several petabytes of historical, structured transaction data in Apache Avro format on-premises. You are migrating this data to Google Cloud for a machine learning project. You must ensure the data can be accessed for large-scale analysis and model training with BigQuery. You must also minimize storage costs and avoid the overhead of loading the data into BigQuery-managed storage. What should you do?

options.A: Use the BigQuery Data Transfer Service to ingest all Avro files into a BigQuery native table.
options.B: Migrate the data to a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance, and use BigQuery federated queries to access the data.
options.C: Store the data in a Cloud Storage bucket, and define a BigQuery external table partitioned by a relevant column.
options.D: Store the data in a Cloud Storage bucket, define a schema, and then use the bq load command to upload files individually.

questions.question: Your team stores its container images in Artifact Registry. You need to create a new Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster and deploy these containers. An IAM service account with the required permissions to pull images from Artifact Registry has already been configured. You must make sure that the images can be deployed to the GKE cluster. What should you do?

options.A: In the Pod manifest, enter the service account name in the serviceAccountName field.
options.B: Enable Workload Identity Federation for GKE on the cluster.
options.C: Deploy the cluster nodes with the specified service account.
options.D: After creating the cluster, store the service account JSON key in a Kubernetes Secret.

questions.question: You manage a business-critical backend application that runs on a Compute Engine managed instance group (MIG). The operations team needs a near-real-time notification when the average CPU utilization across every instance in the MIG exceeds 75% continuously for five minutes. You need to implement a scalable Google Cloud solution that fulfills this monitoring requirement. What should you do?

options.A: Create a logs-based metric in Cloud Logging that filters for high CPU usage entries, and then create a Cloud Monitoring alert policy based on that custom metric.
options.B: Deploy the Ops Agent to all Compute Engine VM instances to collect the CPU metric. Use a custom script running on a separate Compute Engine instance to poll this metric every five minutes, and send an email notification if the threshold is breached.
options.C: Create a Cloud Monitoring alerting policy that targets the compute.googleapis.com/instance/cpu/utilization metric. Set the threshold to 75% and the duration to five minutes.
options.D: Configure an autoscaling policy for the MIG to use a CPU utilization target of 75% for five minutes, and then enable a notification channel in the autoscaler settings.

questions.question: You manage a fleet of data storage solutions for your company on Google Cloud, including Bigtable, Cloud SQL, Memorystore, and Spanner. You need one unified view to monitor the health of every data storage solution and identify any that are at risk of downtime. What should you do?

options.A: Use Dataplex Universal Catalog to search the metadata of the data storage solutions to obtain the required insights.
options.B: Use the terraform state list command in the directory used to deploy the data storage solutions.
options.C: In the Google Cloud Console, use Cloud Asset Inventory to see an overview of the data storage solutions.
options.D: In the Google Cloud Console, navigate to Database Center to find an overview of the data storage solutions.

questions.question: You are deploying a new application on a Compute Engine VM instance. The application must store operational logs in a Cloud Storage bucket named `project-logs-us-central1` and be able to create new objects (logs) in that bucket. It must be restricted from modifying or deleting existing objects and from accessing any other buckets in the Google Cloud project. You must configure access according to the principle of least privilege. What should you do?

options.A: Create a dedicated service account for the application. Grant this service account the predefined roles/storage.objectCreator IAM role on the project-logs-us-central1 Cloud Storage bucket. Attach the service account to the Compute Engine VM instance.
options.B: Grant the Compute Engine default service account the predefined roles/storage.objectAdmin IAM role on the Google Cloud project.
options.C: Create a dedicated service account for the application. Generate a service account key, and grant the service account the predefined roles/storage.adm in IAM role on the project-logs-us-central1 Cloud Storage bucket. Store the key file on the Compute Engine VM.
options.D: Grant the Compute Engine default service account the predefined roles/storage.objectCreator IAM role on the Google Cloud project. Attach the service account to the Compute Engine VM instance.

questions.question: You are establishing a standard process to manage team access to hundreds of Google Cloud resources. Your organization uses Cloud Identity as its primary identity provider, and you want to base access on team membership. You need a solution that makes granting and revoking access easier as individuals join and leave teams. The solution must minimize administrative effort and follow Google-recommended security practices. What should you do?

options.A: For each team, create a Google Group in Cloud Identity with the cloudidentity.googleapis.com/groups.discussion_forum group property label. Add team members to the group, and use the group in IAM policies.
options.B: For each team, create a service account. Grant each team member the IAM permission to impersonate that service account.
options.C: For each team, create a service account. Grant each team member the IAM permission to generate and download keys for that service account.
options.D: For each team, create a Google Group in Cloud Identity with the cloudidentity.googleapis.com/groups.discussion_forum and cloudidentity.googleapis.com/groups.security group property labels. Add team members to the group, and use the group in IAM policies.

questions.question: You are a Google Cloud organization policy administrator for a company operating in a regulated industry. You must enforce a policy that restricts all new location-based Google Cloud resources to only the `australia-southeast1` and `australia-southeast2` regions. You want this policy to require minimal configuration. What should you do?

options.A: Create a custom organization policy that uses the resource.location == ‘australia-southeast1’ || resource.location == ‘australia-southeast2’ Common Expression Language (CEL) condition.
options.B: Modify the gcp.resourceLocations list constraint by adding in:australia-locations to the allowed_values list.
options.C: Modify the gcp.resourceLocations list constraint by adding in:australia-locations to the denied_values list.
options.D: Create a custom organization policy that uses the resource.location.startsWith(‘australia’) Common Expression Language (CEL) condition.

questions.question: You are building and deploying an application on Cloud Run that uses Cloud SQL for data storage. You must track how many database connections the application creates to ensure database connections are reused. What should you do?

options.A: In Cloud Monitoring, create a custom metric that tracks the creation of Cloud Run instances, and display the metric on a dashboard.
options.B: Log each new database connection in the application. In Cloud Monitoring, create a custom metric for these logs, and display the metric on a dashboard.
options.C: In the Google Cloud console, navigate to the Cloud SQL instance, and review the instance logs.
options.D: In Cloud Trace, enable trace storage for your project, and use a filter to check for new database connections.

questions.question: A development team has packaged and pushed a new container image to Artifact Registry. Because of design requirements, the application must be able to scale to zero. You need to move this image to production as quickly as possible while meeting those design requirements. What should you do?

options.A: Create an instance template for the container, and use it to create a managed instance group behind an external Application Load Balancer.
options.B: Create an app.yaml file that specifies the container images, and deploy it to the App Engine Flexible environment.
options.C: Write a Kubernetes Deployment and a Service manifest (YAML), and apply them to a Google Kubernetes Engine cluster.
options.D: Deploy the application directly to Cloud Run.

questions.question: You administer Identity and Access Management (IAM) for your Google Cloud project. A new developer has joined the cloud-developer team and needs to deploy containerized applications to an existing Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. They do not need to manage the GKE cluster itself or any other cloud resources. Following the principle of least privilege, what should you do?

options.A: Add the developer to the cloud-developer group that already has the container.developer IAM role.
options.B: Grant the developer the container.admin IAM role for the project.
options.C: Grant the developer the container.serviceAgent IAM role for the project.
options.D: Grant the developer the editor IAM role for the project.

questions.question: You are building a monitoring application that runs on a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. The application needs credentials from a service account to collect performance data. However, your organization has a policy that forbids creating new service account keys. You must give the application access while adhering to Google-recommended security practices. What should you do?

options.A: Use your personal user credentials to authenticate the application, ensuring your account has the necessary permissions.
options.B: Create a new project, generate a service account key in the new project, and grant the service account the required IAM roles in the application project.
options.C: Override the organization policy in the project, and create a long-lived service account key in the GKE cluster.
options.D: Configure Workload Identity Federation to allow the application to impersonate a service account.

questions.question: You are managing a new Google Cloud project for a web application. The web application runs on a Compute Engine VM, and your team has a strict budget. You have already created a Cloud Billing budget and configured an alert rule to send an email when 90% of the budget is used. You must ensure that project spending automatically stops when it exceeds the budgeted amount. What should you do?

options.A: Create a new Cloud Billing account, and associate the project with it to prevent new spending from affecting your project’s budget.
options.B: Create a Pub/Sub topic, and connect it to the budget. Create a Cloud Run function that subscribes to the Pub/Sub topic and executes code to stop the VM.
options.C: Use the Cloud Billing dashboard to identify the forecasted spend of your project, and then update the budget and alert to match the forecasted spend.
options.D: Rely on the budget’s configuration to automatically disable billable resources when the spend reaches 100%.

questions.question: The Human Resources department at your company publishes a BigQuery dataset containing anonymized information about company sales and products. All company employees are managed in the `terramearth.com` Cloud Identity account and must be able to view this dataset as authenticated users. You need to give every employee in the company read-only access to this BigQuery dataset. What should you do?

options.A: Grant the roles/bigquery.dataViewer role to the domain:terramearth.com principal on the dataset’s IAM policy.
options.B: Grant the roles/bigquery.dataViewer role to the allUsers principal on the dataset’s IAM policy.
options.C: Grant the roles/bigquery.dataViewer role to a new service account on the dataset’s IAM policy.
options.D: Grant the roles/bigquery.dataViewer role to the allAuthenticatedUsers principal on the dataset’s IAM policy.

questions.question: An application reads data from a Pub/Sub topic. During local development, you used your personal credentials to authenticate and test the application. You now want to deploy it to Vertex AI and have created a new service account to serve as the application's identity. You need to ensure that the deployed application can continue accessing the Pub/Sub topic. What should you do?

options.A: Grant the relevant IAM roles to the service account used as your agent identity.
options.B: Generate a JSON private key for the service account, and upload the key as Vertex AI metadata.
options.C: Extract your access token by using the gcloud auth print-access-token command, and store it with the application.
options.D: Create a secret in Secret Manager to store your personal credentials, and configure the application’s authentication code to use this secret.

questions.question: You are developing an application on your personal workstation that will be hosted in Google Cloud. You are authenticated with a Google Account (USER). You need to test whether a particular set of permissions assigned to an existing service account (SERVICE_ACCOUNT) is sufficient for a task, without handling sensitive secret information. What should you do?

options.A: Grant USER the IAM role roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser on SERVICE_ACCOUNT.
options.B: Grant USER the IAM role roles/iam.serviceAccountKeyAdmin on SERVICE_ACCOUNT.
options.C: Grant USER the IAM role roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on SERVICE_ACCOUNT.
options.D: Grant USER the IAM role roles/iam.serviceAccountUser on SERVICE_ACCOUNT.
